title: perf(codex): rebuild only codex rows when a new thread appears
context:
A newly spawned Codex thread reaches the corpus signature as a rollout
day-dir mtime bump, because Codex nests rollouts by date. Dir-granular
extras changes were routed to the full-rebuild path, which is
deliberately kept off the request path, so the new session could not
appear until a background O(all-rows) rebuild finished and a later poll
picked up the snapshot. Measured on a loaded machine: 49.6s from spawn
to the row existing in a built list, with the sidebar showing "spawning"
the whole t
decision: Changed server.py, tests/test_codex_title_freshness.py, tests/test_perf_budget.py: added _archive_codex_extra_keys, CodexSignatureExtraKeysTests, setUpClass, test_every_codex_key_is_one_the_signature_tracks, test_the_rollout_day_dirs_are_included, test_archive_signature_delta_engine_churn_is_engine_scoped_refresh; removed test_archive_signature_delta_hermes_churn_is_engine_scoped_refresh.
consequences: Removes test_archive_signature_delta_hermes_churn_is_engine_scoped_refresh — potential breaking change for callers.
